Assert that a panel is balanced, or has no gaps

Source: R/expect_balanced.R
expect_balanced.Rd

A checkpoint for register panels: every unit (person, company, workplace) must be observed in every period. Missing unit-periods are the violation set, so a failure lists exactly which units lack which periods. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

expect_balanced(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  periods = NULL,
  gaps_only = FALSE,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL,
  log = getOption("daos.check_log"),
  dump = getOption("daos.check_dump")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr or c(cvr, lbnr).

time

The period column (one column), e.g. year. Any type that sorts, such as integer years or dates.

periods

Expected periods. Defaults to the periods observed in data.

gaps_only

If FALSE (default), every unit must be observed in every period. If TRUE, only periods between a unit's first and last observation are required.

success_msg

Message shown (and logged) when data is empty. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the log names every check that ran, and "The dataset is empty." otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown (and logged) when unit-periods are missing and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when data is not empty. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

log

Optional path to a log file. The directory is created automatically. Defaults to getOption("daos.check_log").

dump

Optional directory. When the check fails, the offending rows are written there as a timestamped CSV file (UTF-8 with BOM, so Excel reads æøå correctly). Defaults to getOption("daos.check_dump").

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

Register populations are rarely fully balanced: people are born, die and migrate, and firms open and close. gaps_only = TRUE relaxes the rule to what usually should hold: a unit may enter late and leave early, but once present it must not skip a period between its first and last. A person present in 2019 and 2021 but missing in 2020 is then a gap; a person first seen in 2021 is not.

What counts as a period

By default the expected periods are those observed anywhere in the data. A period missing for every unit (e.g. a year that was never loaded) is therefore invisible. Pass the periods you expect, e.g. periods = 2015:2024, to catch that too. Observations outside periods are ignored, as are rows with a missing period.

Duplicated unit-periods do not make a panel unbalanced, but they are usually an error of their own: check them with expect_unique()(data, id, time).

The check scales to full-population registers: the unit-period grid is only built for units that actually lack a period.

See also

expect_unique() for duplicated unit-periods, expect_no_overlap() for spell data, expect_empty().

Examples

panel <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c"),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2022, 2022)
)

# Not balanced: b lacks 2021, c lacks 2020 and 2021
expect_balanced(panel, cpr, year)
#> Warning: Panel is not balanced: missing cpr-year combinations
#> ℹ 3 rows found:
#>   cpr = "b", year = 2021
#>   cpr = "c", year = 2020
#>   cpr = "c", year = 2021

# Only gaps: b lacks 2021; c simply entered in 2022
expect_balanced(panel, cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE)
#> Warning: Gaps in panel: missing cpr-year combinations
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>   cpr = "b", year = 2021

# A year missing for everyone is only found with explicit periods
expect_balanced(panel, cpr, year, periods = 2019:2022, gaps_only = TRUE)
#> Warning: Gaps in panel: missing cpr-year combinations
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>   cpr = "b", year = 2021
